sentence: A 44-year-old male, originally from Mali, attended the Emergency Department due to a six-hour history of fever and general malaise.
His history of interest includes Graves-Basedow disease treated with carbimazole 30 mg/day for 6 weeks and the extraction of the lower third molar four days ago.
The physical examination revealed blood pressure of 39.5oC, blood pressure of 122/71 and heart rate of 137 l/min.
In the mouth, cavities were observed in several teeth and redness in the area of ​​tooth extraction, with the rest of the examination being unremarkable.
The blood test showed 500 leukocytes/mm3 (0% neutrophils) with the rest of the series normal, CRP 321 mg/dL, normalized thyroid function and no other data of interest.
Urine, sputum and blood samples are taken for microbiological study and broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment is started (amikacin 20 mg/kg/day and cefepime 2 g/8 hours).

In the bone marrow study carried out the next day, hypercellularity with maturation arrest was detected in myeloid series, with no other data of interest, of probable pharmacological etiology, which is why carbimazole was suspended and treatment with G-CSF was started 5 µ/kg/d.

The first three days of admission, the patient had two episodes of fever of 39oC, so on the fourth day the previous antibiotic treatment was changed to meropenem 1 g/8 hours and fluconazole 400 mg/day was added, at the same time that Transesophageal echocardiogram ruled out the presence of endocarditis.

On the fifth day the fever disappeared, coinciding with the partial recovery of the neutrophil count to 1,800/mm3, and on the seventh day he was discharged due to favorable progress and resolution of the condition.

After 18 hours of incubation, the growth of a gram-negative bacillus was detected in the aerobic and anaerobic blood cultures, which were subsequently subcultured in different solid media in aerobiosis, anaerobiosis and in an atmosphere enriched in CO2.
After 48 hours, some pale yellow colonies grew on Columbia Agar, Chocolate Agar and Brucella Agar (not on McConkey medium), embedded in the agar and with a hypochlorite odor.
These colonies were oxidase positive, catalase negative, urease and indole negative, reduced nitrates to nitrites and did not ferment carbohydrates.

In the sensitivity study that was carried out in parallel by the Kirby-Bauer method with Mueller-Hinton blood plates and with E-Test® AB BIODISK, the isolated strain was sensitive to all the antibiotics tested (ampicillin, amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, azithromycin, levofloxacin, ciprofloxacin, cefotaxime, cefuroxime, imipenen, cotrimoxazole and tetracyclines), except for gentamicin and amikacin, with MICs of 16 and 32 µg/mL, respectively.
His identity was confirmed by sequencing of the 16s gene.
